The incident matters greatly to the local community due to the sudden loss of life and severe injuries sustained near a heavily trafficked public transit area. Local authorities continue to evaluate the situation as the investigation into the cause of the crash proceeds.

stories.title: World Leaders Gather at COP31 in Turkiye to Debate Climate Goals
stories.summary:
World leaders are gathering in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, Turkiye, for the COP31 climate summit to outline their priorities and push for new agreements to combat global warming. Negotiators are focusing heavily on increasing the share of electricity in global energy use and reviving stalled international efforts to transition away from fossil fuels, despite rising greenhouse gas emissions and competing geopolitical crises.

Former French Prime Minister Laurent Fabius noted that the leaders' speeches aim to provide crucial political momentum for the negotiations. The conference schedule features rapid-fire addresses from numerous high-ranking officials, including Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine. The United States is absent from the summit for the second consecutive year following President Donald Trump's withdrawal from climate cooperation.

Host nation Turkiye has advocated for a central target aiming to raise electricity's share of total global energy consumption to 35% by 2035. However, critics point out that the proposal lacks mandates for clean energy generation and definitive plans to phase out coal, oil, and gas. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged countries to establish clear timelines for moving away from fossil fuels.

This summit follows previous challenges, such as the prior COP in Brazil failing to reach a consensus on reducing fossil fuel dependency. The ongoing discussions are critical as a recent United Nations report warns the world is on track to surpass the 1.5 degrees Celsius warming limit set under the Paris Agreement.

stories.title: New Zealand Includes Injured Trio in Strong Test Squad for India
stories.summary:
New Zealand Cricket announced a strong test squad on Wednesday for the upcoming series against India, selecting Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, and Tom Blundell despite ongoing fitness doubts. All three players are targeting full recovery ahead of the first test match next week.

Opening batsman Conway is recovering from a concussion sustained during a training collision with fast bowler Matt Henry. All-rounder Ravindra has been sidelined since dislocating his shoulder while filming a promotional catch in September, missing both the ODI and Twenty20 series against India. Wicketkeeper-batsman Blundell is recovering from a quadricep injury, having played just one domestic match since June. The squad also features fast bowler Jacob Duffy, while players like Zak Foulkes, Will O'Rourke, and Ben Sears are absent due to injuries. Kane Williamson retired from international cricket following the team's 2-1 series victory in England last June.

Coach Rob Walter noted that the roster remains largely consistent with the group that toured England. He expressed enthusiasm about reuniting the team and welcoming home crowds.

The two-match series begins next Wednesday with the first test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, followed by the second test at the Hagley Oval in Christchurch starting on November 27. The selected squad is captained by Tom Latham and includes Blundell, Conway, Duffy, Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Ravindra, Mitchell Santner, Nathan Smith, Blair Tickner, and Will Young.

stories.title: بانئ پی ٹی آئی کا رات گئے پمز اسپتال میں طبی معائنہ مکمل
stories.summary: بانئ پی ٹی آئی کو سخت سیکیورٹی حصار میں 10 اور 11 نومبر کی درمیانی شب اڈیالہ جیل سے اسلام آباد کے پمز اسپتال منتقل کیا گیا۔ جیل ذرائع اور اسپتال انتظامیہ کے جاری کردہ اعلامیے کے مطابق اس دورے کا مقصد ان کا تفصیلی طبی معائنہ اور آنکھوں کا فالو اپ علاج کرنا تھا۔ پمز اسپتال کے ماہرین نے ان کے بلڈ پریشر اور آنکھوں کا معائنہ کیا جبکہ امراض چشم کی ٹیم نے ان کی دائیں آنکھ میں ایک اینٹی وی ای جی ایف انجکشن بھی لگایا۔ معائنے کے دوران ان کی تمام اہم طبی علامات معمول کے مطابق پائیں گئیں اور ان کی مجموعی جسمانی حالت کو تسلی بخش اور مستحکم قرار دیا گیا۔ طبی کارروائی اور معائنہ مکمل ہونے کے فوری بعد انہیں واپس اڈیالہ جیل منتقل کر دیا گیا جہاں ان کی بہن روبینہ خان اور بیٹے قاسم خان نے کانفرنس روم میں ان سے ملاقات کی۔ اس دوران سیکیورٹی کے انتہائی سخت انتظامات کیے گئے تھے جبکہ حکام کی جانب سے اس پورے عمل کی نگرانی کی گئی۔

stories.title: PM Shehbaz Sharif Arrives in Turkiye for COP31 Climate Summit
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Turkiye to attend the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) World Leaders' Summit in Antalya. Accompanied by PPP leader Senator Sherry Rehman, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, and Adviser Tariq Fatemi, the premier is scheduled to address the high-level segment to advocate for climate justice.

During his visit, Prime Minister Shehbaz will participate in a high-level session titled "Clean Energy Transition by 2035: Powering the Future", which is hosted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The prime minister is expected to present Pakistan's national statement, address renewable energy visions, hold bilateral meetings with world leaders, and attend a gala dinner hosted by President Erdogan.

Pakistan consistently urges developed nations to deliver greater financial and technical assistance to developing countries vulnerable to climate impacts. Contributing less than one per cent of global greenhouse gas emissions, Pakistan faces a disproportionate share of climate-induced damage and has long pushed for predictable and accessible climate finance, as well as the operationalization of the Loss and Damage Fund established during COP27 in Egypt.

stories.title: Afghan National Arrested in Tirah Valley for Plotting Terrorist Attacks in Pakistan
stories.summary:
Security forces and law enforcement agencies in Pakistan arrested an Afghan national during a joint intelligence-based operation in the Tirah Valley on November 7. Additional Inspector General Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Abbas Ahsan, speaking at a press conference alongside Information Secretary Mahmood Jan Babar, identified the suspect as Hikmatullah, also known as Hamza. According to officials, the suspect originated from Afghanistan's Paktia province and was apprehended near Peshawar utilizing human intelligence and electronic surveillance.

Authorities stated that the suspect previously served in the former Afghan national army, undergoing three months of standard military training followed by three months of commando training. Following the dissolution of the Afghan army, he utilized his expertise at various madrassas to facilitate terrorist activities inside Pakistan, including the preparation of a suicide bomber named Akrama at a facility near Jalalabad. Investigators also linked the suspect to the former Gul Bahadur group, noting he had served as a security guard for a local commander.

Officials highlighted that the suspect's interrogation exposed broader militant networks, identifying local and cross-border facilitators as well as targeted attack locations. During the briefing, authorities also played a recorded video statement from the arrested individual detailing his background and involvement. Information Secretary Babar emphasized that Afghan territory continues to be exploited for cross-border terrorism, warning that Pakistani security forces remain fully prepared to block and neutralize any threats.

This arrest occurs against a backdrop of escalating security challenges in Pakistan, where data from monitoring organizations like ACLED indicates a sharp rise in militant violence since 2022. Provincial reports in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have similarly documented a significant surge in terrorist incidents, with security personnel frequently targeted. Islamabad has consistently urged the Afghan Taliban administration to prevent militant groups such as the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan from utilizing Afghan soil to launch attacks, a concern echoed in recent United Nations findings.

stories.title: Asad Mehmood Fails to Appear Before NAB Over Pakistan Post Scandal
stories.summary:
Asad Mehmood, the former federal minister for communication and son of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rahman, failed to appear before the National Accountability Bureau on Monday. He had been summoned by the anti-graft watchdog to explain his position regarding alleged irregularities during his 2022-23 tenure.

The investigation centers on 4,252 appointments made at Pakistan Post, which exceeded the Establishment Division's authorized recruitment limit of 3,938 posts. The bureau is examining allegations that 2,646 of these appointments violated cabinet committee directions by filling posts that had already been abolished. Additional scrutiny involves permanent appointments made despite recommendations for contractual hires, potential political affiliations of selected candidates, forged documents, over-age candidates, and domicile quota violations.

NAB officials remained tight-lipped regarding their next steps, though standard procedure often involves issuing second and third notices before considering punitive actions such as arrest. A senior official declined to disclose specific investigation details to the media, citing new laws that restrict sharing information prior to a court decision.

The case highlights ongoing scrutiny of political figures and public sector recruitment practices in Pakistan. The investigation underscores accountability efforts concerning administrative decisions made during past government terms.

stories.title: Indian Rupee Aims for Rally Extension on Lower Oil Prices
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee is positioned to extend its recent market rally, supported by a significant drop in international crude oil prices and previous intervention by the Reserve Bank of India. Traders anticipated the currency to open between 93.70 and 93.74 against the dollar, following a close of 93.93275 on Monday after Indian financial markets were closed for a local holiday.

Brent crude slid below $90 a barrel for the first time since August after US officials downplayed the necessity of further military action against Iran, easing fears of Middle Eastern supply disruptions. Although prices recovered slightly from their lows of $92.20, they remained down significantly over the week, offering the rupee relief from a major pressure point. Previously, high crude prices forced the RBI to open a special window for oil refiners to secure dollars outside the open market.

The rupee has recovered more than 3% from recent lows due to RBI efforts and foreign equity inflows as global investors diversify away from concentrated artificial intelligence-related shares. However, analysts note that the current exchange rate levels make importing attractive once again, potentially increasing dollar demand.

Adding a note of caution, US Treasury yields surged on Tuesday following data showing that US consumer prices rose faster than expected in October. This inflation data led traders to increase bets on a larger interest rate hike during the Federal Reserve's upcoming December meeting, acting as a potential dampener on the rupee's upward momentum.

stories.title: Usman Khawaja Denies Witch Hunt Amid Calls to Reopen Ball-Tampering Probe
stories.summary:
Former Australia opening batsman Usman Khawaja has denied that his recent revelations regarding the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal were intended to launch a witch hunt. Speaking on ABC, Khawaja maintained that he was merely sharing his version of the truth and seeking team accountability rather than calling for new investigations.

In his newly released autobiography titled "Sabr", Khawaja claimed that the ball-tampering plot during the South Africa series was common knowledge throughout the entire team, contradicting Cricket Australia's original 2018 inquiry which concluded that only David Warner, Steve Smith, and Cameron Bancroft had prior knowledge of the cheating. Former teammate David Warner publicly backed Khawaja's statements as entirely accurate, noting that the truth has finally come out.

Despite the renewed debate sparked by the book, Cricket Australia Chief Todd Greenberg ruled out reopening the investigation, stating there was no compelling reason for a new probe. Other figures involved in the 2018 series, including former captain Pat Cummins, bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon, and coach Darren Lehmann, have previously denied widespread player awareness of the incident.

stories.title: US Dollar Holds Near Two-Week High Amid Inflation and Fed Rate Hike Bets
stories.summary: The United States dollar maintained positions close to a two-week high during early Asian trading on Wednesday, driven by hotter-than-expected inflation data and hawkish statements from Federal Reserve officials. The US dollar index measured steady at 102.22, nearing its strongest level since October 28 following a 0.5% increase on Tuesday. The currency movement came after reports revealed that consumer prices in October climbed higher than anticipated due to rising costs for food and accommodation. This economic indicator prompted traders to reevaluate monetary policy, with market participants nearly abandoning expectations that the central bank will pause at its upcoming policy meeting concluding on December 9. According to CME Group's FedWatch tool, fed funds futures priced in a 91.9% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike, increasing from 84% the previous day, while a smaller contingent priced in a potential 50-basis-point adjustment or subsequent January increase. Analysts like Chris Weston from Pepperstone Group Ltd noted that the rates market is actively questioning how restrictive policy must ultimately become, posing a significant debate for risk assets. Meanwhile, major currencies showed mixed performance, with the euro and British pound flat at $1.1168 and $1.3345 respectively, while the US dollar remained unchanged against the Japanese yen at 158.715. The Australian dollar nudged up 0.1% to $0.6870, and the New Zealand dollar held flat at $0.5605. Concurrently, US 10-year Treasury bond yields rose 13.8 basis points to 4.996%. In cryptocurrency markets, bitcoin traded down 0.3% at $73,566.45, and ether dropped 0.5% to $2,044.61, both lingering near three-month lows.

stories.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Houthi Missiles While Airstrikes Hit Sanaa
stories.summary: The Saudi-led military coalition reported intercepting multiple missiles and a drone fired by Yemen’s Houthi movement towards various Saudi cities on Tuesday, while Houthi-controlled media detailed retaliatory air strikes hitting the Yemeni capital of Sanaa. The coalition confirmed shooting down a ballistic missile and a cruise missile targeting Riyadh, alongside another ballistic missile aimed at the kingdom's southern region and a drone detected over the eastern territory. Civil defense authorities issued alerts in Riyadh, Abha, and Khamis Mushait before confirming that threats had subsided. Early morning explosions were heard by AFP journalists, and residents received emergency mobile shelter notifications. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for strikes on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and an oil facility in Abqaiq, though Saudi authorities provided no immediate commentary. In Sanaa, the Saba news agency stated that Saudi air strikes struck a petrol station in the Jadar district and a state oil company building in the southern sector. This military escalation follows a recent Houthi attack on an Aramco skyscraper in Riyadh’s financial district and disputes regarding the East-West Pipeline in Madina province. In response to ongoing security measures, Riyadh authorities shifted schoolchildren back to online learning for Tuesday, continuing precautionary protocols. The recurring attacks create headwinds for Saudi Arabia's broader economic diversification strategies aimed at drawing foreign investments and tourism. Images released by the Saudi Press Agency on Tuesday highlighted visible damage on several floors of the Aramco Tower, prompting regional condemnation and renewed calls for security stability.
